edition.name: Saturday edition

presentation.ear_right: Inside: the minister spared a censure, the G7 diesel release, France's school revolt

edition.note: Built from headlines and RSS descriptions published between 05:30 on 30 September and 05:30 on 3 October, 3,891 articles. 128 of 132 feeds at 17 publishers polled; four Financial Times section feeds failed.

stories.headline: DTU hack may expose data on up to 200,000 people
stories.deck: CPR numbers and names may be among the data taken; the attack is contained and reported to Datatilsynet.
extended: Hackers took 'a large amount of data' from the user database of the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), the university said in a statement on Friday. Up to 200,000 current and former staff, students, guests and partners may be affected.

The data may include CPR numbers and full names, and for active users home addresses and phone numbers. The database reaches back to 2003 and holds about 40,000 active and 160,000 former users. DTU cannot yet say exactly what was taken or how many people are affected.

The intruders compromised several DTU profiles to reach the database. DTU contained the attack on Friday morning and has reported it to Datatilsynet; the National Unit for Special Crime (NSK) is in dialogue with the university.
DTU warns that the data could be used for identity misuse and to make phishing more credible. People whose CPR number it holds will be told via e-Boks.
Old IT systems and large amounts of personal data make universities vulnerable, Jens Myrup Pedersen, professor of cybersecurity at Aarhus University, tells Ritzau.
standard: Hackers took 'a large amount of data' from the user database of the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), the university said in a statement on Friday. Up to 200,000 current and former staff, students, guests and partners may be affected.
The data may include CPR numbers and full names, and for active users home addresses and phone numbers. DTU cannot yet say exactly what was taken.
DTU contained the attack on Friday morning and has reported it to Datatilsynet. People whose CPR number it holds will be told via e-Boks.
short: Hackers took 'a large amount of data' from the user database of the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), the university said on Friday. Up to 200,000 current and former users may be affected, and CPR numbers and names may be among the data.

callouts.text: This is a serious attack on DTU, and we deeply regret the uncertainty it creates for the people whose information may be affected.
callouts.attribution: Bjarke Bak Christensen, university director at DTU

callouts.text: The question is which accounts have had access to all this personal data, and how well they are protected.
callouts.attribution: Jens Myrup Pedersen, professor of cybersecurity at Aarhus University

stories.headline: Bruus is spared a rebuke as the government's support parties refuse to back one
stories.deck: The Defence Command admitted on Thursday that soldiers fired shots while a Norwegian passenger plane flew overhead.
standard: Jeppe Bruus, the defence minister, will not receive a 'næse', the Folketing's symbolic rebuke, over errors in the Defence Command's account of the drone incidents. Enhedslisten and Alternativet, the government's two support parties, will not back one, which leaves several centre-right parties led by Dansk Folkeparti without the votes.
On Thursday the Defence Command admitted that Danish soldiers fired shots while a Norwegian passenger plane flew over Borris firing range in September 2025. It denies firing at the plane.
Eva Flyvholm, Enhedslisten's defence spokesperson, said a rebuke 'solves nothing' because Bruus was not minister at the time.
short: Jeppe Bruus, the defence minister, will not receive the Folketing's symbolic rebuke over errors in the Defence Command's drone account. Enhedslisten and Alternativet will not back one, so the parties led by Dansk Folkeparti lack the votes.

stories.headline: G7 agrees to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil
stories.deck: The release follows Trump's threat to ban diesel exports to Europe; the G7 agree not to restrict energy exports among themselves.
standard: The G7 countries will release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil through the International Energy Agency over four months, starting immediately, with a large diesel release in the first 20 days. Emmanuel Macron, France's president, announced it on Friday after a video meeting of G7 leaders.
It follows Donald Trump raising the possibility on Wednesday of banning diesel exports to Europe. The G7 countries have agreed not to restrict energy exports among themselves.
Jens Nærvig Pedersen, commodity analyst at Danske Bank, tells Ritzau the release may take the top off diesel prices in Denmark but does not solve the supply crisis.
short: The G7 countries will release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil over four months, Emmanuel Macron, France's president, announced on Friday. It follows Donald Trump raising the possibility on Wednesday of banning diesel exports to Europe.

stories.headline: French school protests spread across the country as pupils vow to keep going
stories.deck: There have been nearly 2,000 arrests; 564 upper-secondary schools are affected.
standard: Pupils in France say they will keep protesting after Edouard Geffrey, the education minister, met their organisations on Friday.

The protests began on 21 September in deprived suburbs around Paris and have spread across the country. There have been nearly 2,000 arrests, and 564 of the country's 3,700 upper-secondary schools are affected. On Friday the authorities closed 400 of them and banned demonstrations.

Geffrey has withdrawn a proposal for higher fees at some institutions of higher education, which helped set off the unrest. The pupils' demands centre on absent teachers who are not replaced, crumbling buildings and classes of up to 36.
short: Pupils in France say they will keep protesting after meeting Edouard Geffrey, the education minister, on Friday. The protests began in the suburbs of Paris on 21 September and have spread across the country, with nearly 2,000 arrests and 564 upper-secondary schools affected.

stories.headline: YouTube brothers' company fined 140,000 kroner over vodka-smuggling video
stories.deck: The Consumer Ombudsman had sought 250,000 kroner; the case also covered undeclared paid promotion for KiMs.
standard: Kender Du Det ApS, the company of the YouTube brothers Elias and Oskar Hole, was fined 140,000 kroner on Friday for several breaches of the Marketing Practices Act.

The case centred on a 2023 video showing their more than 310,000 followers eight ways to smuggle alcohol into festivals, and on undeclared paid promotion for KiMs. The Consumer Ombudsman had sought 250,000 kroner. The company must also pay the costs of the case.

Miriam Michaelsen, a lawyer and chair of Medierådet for Børn og Unge, the media council for children and young people, tells Kristeligt Dagblad that the ruling shows influencers bear a responsibility, and expects more such cases.
short: Kender Du Det ApS, the company of the YouTube brothers Elias and Oskar Hole, was fined 140,000 kroner on Friday for breaches of the Marketing Practices Act, including over a video about smuggling alcohol into festivals.

stories.headline: Municipalities ask for 30 to 40 million kroner a year for shortcut ferries
lede: Ten municipalities behind Denmark's eight municipally run shortcut ferries ask in an open letter for a fixed annual pool of 30 to 40 million kroner in the 2027 finance bill.

stories.headline: Government plans 150 million kroner for training daycare staff
lede: The government plans to spend 150 million kroner in the 2027 budget on training staff in nurseries and kindergartens, half of the 300 million kroner it aims at children's services.

stories.headline: Government and two parties set aside 100 million kroner for rural public transport
lede: The government, Enhedslisten and Alternativet plan to distribute 100 million kroner for public transport, particularly in rural areas, including 3 million kroner to bring Rejsekort to Bornholm, the ministry said on Friday.

stories.headline: Government wins backing to demand lower EU budget
lede: Venstre, De Konservative and Liberal Alliance on Friday backed the government's demand for a marked cut to the proposed spending level in the EU's 2028-2034 budget, accepting it may exceed the current one.

stories.headline: Three parties warn government of agreement breach over packaging fees
lede: Enhedslisten, Alternativet and De Konservative say a bill for a fixed cap on producers' packaging payments to municipalities would breach their 2022 agreement, and demand negotiations.

stories.headline: KL: Denmark will miss 2035 goal for ending gas boilers
lede: Denmark will miss its 2035 goal of ending gas boilers in private homes at the current pace, KL, the municipalities' association, says; the 12 district heating projects expected this year would replace 2,312 boilers.

stories.headline: Greenland halts alcohol sales in Kujalleq Municipality
lede: Naalakkersuisut, Greenland's government, temporarily banned the sale and serving of alcohol in Kujalleq Municipality in south Greenland from Friday, at the municipal council's request, until the order is lifted.

stories.headline: Four charged with killing 37-year-old man in Greenland
lede: Four people, two women aged 22 and 43 and two men aged 18, have been charged with killing a 37-year-old man found dead in Nanortalik in southern Greenland on Thursday.

stories.headline: Police examine whether two assaults on young women in Risskov are linked
lede: East Jutland Police are investigating whether assaults on a 22-year-old woman on 12 July and a 24-year-old runner on 28 September in Risskov near Aarhus are linked, and advise against a private patrol group.

stories.headline: Four right-of-centre parties want grounds for police report against Siddique examined
lede: A motion from four right-of-centre parties, due before Copenhagen's city council on 8 October, seeks an examination of whether to report Sikandar Siddique, Frie Grønne's leader, to police over his residence case.

stories.headline: Syd for Solen festival takes a break in 2027
lede: Syd for Solen, the Copenhagen music festival, takes a break in 2027 because it cannot guarantee its high standard, its organisers said on Friday; they aim to return in 2028.

stories.headline: Magdalena Andersson gets a new attempt to form a Swedish government
lede: Andreas Norlén, the Riksdag speaker, let Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrat leader, resume her attempt to form a Swedish government on Friday, after she had given up on Monday.

stories.headline: US adds 29,000 jobs in September, far short of expectations
lede: The US added 29,000 jobs outside agriculture in September, far short of expectations, and unemployment rose to 4.2 per cent, figures published on Friday show.

stories.headline: Widdecombe murder suspect charged with planning terror against Farage
lede: British counter-terrorism police on Friday charged Joshua Kerry, 28, already accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe, with preparing acts of terrorism including against Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader.

stories.headline: Zelensky says Putin ordered military to abandon rules of war
lede: Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times on Thursday that Ukrainian intelligence shows Vladimir Putin ordered his military leaders in September to disregard the rules of war, a claim not independently verified.

stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills more than 4,000
lede: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, the deadliest in the country's history, had killed 4,018 people by Friday, with 8,300 confirmed cases across seven provinces, government figures show.

stories.headline: Danish Crown merges business units to focus on Europe
lede: Danish Crown said on Friday it will merge seven of its eight business units and lift the share of its pork processed into finished products from 25 to 50 per cent.
